scope: Logical maker/library/instrument hierarchy versus physical installation and file identity
Usage evidence and mandatory Logic, Ableton, Cubase, and Pro Tools feasibility gates
Initial baseline, first-seen continuity, newly indexed roots, and updates
Inherited metadata, user overrides, suppression, and portable edits
Storage/removal safety and incremental catalog performance
Ordered delivery, research limitations, and plan-only completion boundary
verdict: PASS: no blocking issues for the researched redesign plan; this verdict does not approve implementation as complete.
rationale: The plan directly repairs the entity-model failure: arbitrary directories cannot become verified libraries, while instruments retain parent context and physical files remain separately modeled.
Installed footprint is measured at library-installation level, shared patch payloads are not multiplied, and reclaimable space is distinguished from allocated size and recoverable Trash operations.

Saved inclusion, load observations, recency proxies, coverage windows, and unknown history remain distinct. All four required hosts must have positive and negative fixtures before compatibility or unused-cleanup claims.
Initial inventory and newly indexed locations do not fabricate installation dates; stable identities preserve first-seen values across supported moves, rescans, reconnects, and updates.
Tag inheritance excludes sibling-specific summaries; persistent suppression and explicit user precedence prevent rescans from silently undoing edits.
The performance design separates persistent browsing, inventory, metadata, storage, and usage work, with incremental checkpoints and honest incomplete/offline states.
Delivery begins with identity and usage feasibility, then persistence and hierarchy before enrichment or cleanup. Proprietary host decoding has no unsupported schedule or universal-history promise.
Plugin Station tracking and Spotlight are not treated as proven universal usage sources; source limitations are explicit.
implementation_gate_notes: Each implementation increment still requires its own concrete schema, migration, adapter-boundary, resource-budget, and verification specifications.
The feasibility spike may establish unsupported history scopes; failed or absent evidence must not become unused classifications or permission to remove content.
The UI must preserve partial size/coverage and shared-ownership warnings through search, cleanup filters, and removal review, not only in diagnostics.
limitations: Reviewed the plan, not live proprietary host behavior or adapter correctness.
The plan's linked research was not independently re-executed in this critique.
No product code changed; no user content removed, private projects/logs inspected, or .qa-criteria accessed.
